text: Nvidia’s strong results did not stop the slide: its shares fell 2.9% on Wednesday, the S&P 500 slipped for a fifth day and gold dropped to a one-year low, though the Nasdaq and small caps edged up. Anthropic priced its IPO at US$83, above its range, a sign of solid demand for AI shares (Claude is made by Anthropic). Next: Australian jobs figures at 11:30am today (Thu 19 Nov, Melbourne), Anthropic’s first trade in the early hours of Fri Melbourne time (Nasdaq opens 1:30am), and Thursday’s US close at 8am Fri.

The IMF’s October 2026 Global Financial Stability Report reviewed 14 AI financing deals: about US$300bn of equity and US$650bn of debt, tied to roughly US$1.4tn of future spending commitments flowing back to the investors. It names an AI correction as one of three ‘salient risks’, warning of a ‘triple whammy’: equity falls, debt gets harder to service, and promised revenue fails to arrive.

Drawdown bands are my illustrative assumptions, anchored to the historical episodes below. They are not forecasts. The key lesson from 2008: in a forced-selling phase almost everything falls together, including gold miners. What differs is margin resilience and recovery speed.

Exclusion screen: no company with known direct military or defence-procurement ties (including US DoD cloud contracts or DoD equity/offtake deals), and none of the big platforms you flagged as socially unethical. This is a first pass from public reporting. Supply chains are opaque, so verify with an ethical-investment screen before acting.
